key_insight: COVID-19 vaccination was associated with better overall survival among cancer patients in Northwestern Russia; this was not a drug-discovery study.
clinical_relevance: The findings highlight vaccination coverage and COVID-19 burden as relevant factors in cancer outcomes, without establishing a causal survival benefit.
method: Linked cancer registry, vaccination records, and AI-analyzed chest CT data for 1,144 patients.
Compared survival using Kaplan–Meier analysis and adjusted Cox regression.
Used March and November 2021 landmark analyses to mitigate immortal time bias.
evidence_signal: Vaccination coverage was 6.6%; the primary landmark analysis found 3-year survival of 80.3% versus 45.7% and an adjusted mortality HR of 0.40 (95% CI 0.25–0.64), with an attenuated association in sensitivity analysis.
watch_item: The retrospective design, small vaccinated group, and differences in cancer stage and treatment leave potential residual confounding.
paper_title: COVID-19 vaccination and survival of cancer patients in Northwestern Russia: a historical registry-based cohort study
